features: 22 publication-day features. KEV `vendorProject` names match a dev CVE vendor for **89.8%** of KEV rows (61% of KEV vendors; the unmatched ones are mostly vendors whose CVEs are published by MITRE with vendor 'n/a'). The new KEV-history signal is strong and day-0 safe: in train, CVEs from a vendor with **earlier** KEV entries are exploited at **1.03%** vs **0.10%** for the rest (10×), and they contain **77%** of exploited CVEs while being only 25% of CVEs. The own-entry guard matters for 52 dev CVEs that were in KEV before NVD published them.
protocol: On the same views the best rule ('phrase, then CVSS (CNA)') scores **28.1%** on val, **39.3%** on 2023 and **34.9%** on 2024-H1 at K = 110 (selection score = three-period mean **34.1%**). A random pick gets 3–5%. Each view has only 45–121 exploited CVEs, which is why we average the three periods rather than trust any single one.
lr: Under the three-period rule the selected logistic regression is C = 0.3 with rare categories < 5 grouped (selection 37.8%), essentially tied with C = 0.03 / min_freq 20 (37.6%). All ten settings fall within 33.6–37.8%, so the choice is driven by noise. The chosen setting is strong on 2023 (**53.7%**) but weak on val (**30.9%**) and 2024-H1 (**28.9%, below the best rule's 34.9%**): logistic regression is the least stable model across periods.
hgb: Gradient boosting wins clearly, and its choice does not change under the three-period rule: one-hot of frequent vendors/CNAs/CWEs, learning rate 0.03, 15 leaves, ≥ 100 CVEs per leaf (selection **47.4%**). It scores **47.1%** on val, **39.7% / 55.6%** on the two walk-forward folds and 46.6% in grouped CV, and its **worst period (39.7%) beats the rule's worst (34.9%)**. Target encoding is now seeded (scikit-learn shuffled its internal folds without a seed, so earlier runs differed); one-hot still takes 5 of the top 8 places. Caveat: picking the best of 16 noisy settings is optimistic (the median setting scores 41.2%); the Phase 6 test run gives the honest number.
ci: On validation at K = 110, gradient boosting catches **47.1%** [36–60] of exploited CVEs vs **28.1%** for the best rule: **+19.9 points [+6.7, +33.3], better in 100% of bootstrap resamples**, and **+15.5 points [+1.6, +28.6] over logistic regression** (P = 98%). The selected logistic regression is only +4.5 points over the rule at K = 110 (P = 70%, CI crosses 0) but +16.2 at K = 305 (P = 99%).
curve: Both models sit above both rules across the whole capacity range. At **K = 110 gradient boosting catches 32 of the 68 exploited CVEs where the best rule catches 19**. To match gradient boosting's 47% at K = 110, the best rule needs **520 patches/month, 4.7× the capacity**. Logistic regression stays between the rules and gradient boosting at small K and narrows the gap only at large K.
importance: The models rely on **who** (CNA, vendor, and the vendor's earlier KEV entries), **how bad** (CNA CVSS score, privileges required, attack vector) and, surprisingly, **description length**. Because exploited CVEs' descriptions are edited more often, we tested description length directly: replacing each history-sample CVE's length with its **original** publication-day length leaves val recall unchanged (47.1% → 47.1% at K = 110, 67.6% → 67.6% at K = 305; score rank correlation 0.98). So it is a genuine day-0 signal, likely vendor writing style (e.g. Microsoft's very short titles), not an edit artefact. Dropping it costs ~9 points on val and 2023. Permutation importance on 68 positives is noisy (some LR values are slightly negative); Phase 7 adds SHAP.
final: Structured day-0 features alone already beat every rule. **Gradient boosting: 47.1% at K = 110 and 67.6% at K = 305 on validation** (three-period selection score 47.4%), vs 28.1% / 42.7% for the best rule and 23.7% / 38.3% for the current CVSS rule. It is the only method whose **worst** period (39.7%) stays above the best rule's worst (34.9%). Logistic regression (selection 37.8%) is unstable across periods and loses to the rule on 2024-H1. PR-AUC disagrees with recall@K (the boosting model has the lower PR-AUC, 0.049): PR-AUC rewards the whole ordering, while the team only patches the top ~3% of each month.
